blocks.content: The reverse-proxy topic covered a proxy that sits in front of servers, protecting and representing them to the outside world. A forward proxy does the genuinely opposite job, sitting in front of clients instead, representing them when they reach out to the wider internet.
This distinction, which side of the connection a proxy actually sits on and represents, is exactly what separates these two genuinely different, commonly confused concepts.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437997527-796638402.png
1. The Genuinely Opposite Role From a Reverse Proxy
blocks.text: 1. The Genuinely Opposite Role From a Reverse Proxy

blocks.content: A reverse proxy, covered in the previous topic, sits in front of servers, protecting and representing them. A forward proxy sits in front of clients instead, representing them when they reach out to destinations on the wider internet. Same basic idea, an intermediary standing in front of something, but on the genuinely opposite side of the connection.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437997527-869779305.png
blocks.alt: The Genuinely Opposite Role From a Reverse Proxy

blocks.content: 2. Hiding the Real Client

When a client connects to a destination through a forward proxy, the destination server only ever sees the forward proxy itself, its address, its identity, not the real client actual address or identity behind it. The forward proxy genuinely stands in for the client from the destination point of view.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437998465-244985601.png
3. Enforcing Access Control and Policy

Organizations commonly route all outgoing traffic from their internal network through a forward proxy specifically to enforce content policies, blocking access to certain sites or categories of content for every single user on that network, all controlled and enforced centrally at one single point.

4. Caching at the Forward Proxy Too
blocks.text: 4. Caching at the Forward Proxy Too

blocks.content: Exactly like a reverse proxy can cache content, a forward proxy can cache commonly requested external content too. If many different users within an organization request the exact same external resource, the forward proxy can serve it directly from its own cache, meaning genuinely less repeated external traffic actually leaving the organization network.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437998467-425244420.png
blocks.alt: Caching at the Forward Proxy Too

blocks.content: 5. A Genuine Anonymity and Privacy Use
blocks.text: 5. A Genuine Anonymity and Privacy Use

blocks.content: Connecting directly to a destination naturally reveals the real client own address to that destination. Connecting through a forward proxy instead means the destination only ever sees the proxy own address, not the real client behind it, a real, practical privacy benefit some tools and services deliberately rely on.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437998467-779662046.png
blocks.alt: A Genuine Anonymity and Privacy Use

blocks.title: A genuinely real, practical use, not just a theoretical one
blocks.content: Some tools and services people actually use daily rely specifically on this exact mechanism, deliberately routing traffic through a forward proxy to keep a user own real address from being directly visible to whatever they are connecting to.
6. A Real World Analogy

A person using a mail forwarding service captures this well. Mail gets sent to the forwarding service own address first, which then privately redirects it on to the person real, private address behind the scenes. The original sender only ever sees the forwarding service address, never the real, private destination.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437998467-328467011.png

blocks.title: A simple memory trick worth keeping
blocks.content: A reverse proxy works in reverse of the normal flow, from the server side, protecting what is behind it. A forward proxy forwards traffic on behalf of the client in front of it. The names genuinely describe which side each one sits on.
7. The Two Proxy Types, Side by Side, One Final Time
blocks.text: 7. The Two Proxy Types, Side by Side, One Final Time

blocks.content: A reverse proxy represents and protects servers, sitting between the outside world and the real backend infrastructure. A forward proxy represents and protects clients, sitting between an internal user and the wider outside internet. Genuinely opposite roles, both built on the exact same underlying idea of an intermediary standing in front of something.

items: Confusing a forward proxy with a reverse proxy, remembering which side of the connection each one actually represents is the entire key to keeping them straight.
Assuming a forward proxy is only ever used for blocking content, when caching and genuine privacy or anonymity are just as real, common uses.
A forward proxy sits in front of clients, representing them to the wider internet, the destination never sees the real client directly.
It is commonly used for centrally enforced access control, caching, and genuine privacy or anonymity.
A reverse proxy protects servers; a forward proxy protects clients, remembering this distinction is the single most useful takeaway from both topics.
